rows.label: Domain Name
rows.value: A human-readable label for a location on the internet (e.g. meridian-financial.com). NOT a website — an address. One domain can have dozens of subdomains pointing to different services on different servers.

rows.label: IP Address
rows.value: The numerical label computers actually use to route traffic (e.g. 104.22.7.45 IPv4; 2606:4700::1 IPv6). Domain names are for humans. IP addresses are for machines.

rows.label: DNS
rows.value: Domain Name System — the global infrastructure that translates domain names to IP addresses. Hierarchy: Root Nameserver → TLD Nameserver → Authoritative Nameserver. All records are publicly queryable.

rows.label: Subdomain
rows.value: A prefix added to a registered domain (dev.meridian-financial.com). Created in DNS by the domain owner — no separate registration needed. Discoverable through Certificate Transparency logs.

sections.heading: DNS Record Types and What They Reveal

rows.label: A Record
rows.value: Maps domain to IPv4 address. Always follow with an IP WHOIS lookup. If IP belongs to Cloudflare/Akamai/AWS — you're seeing a CDN, not the target's actual server.

rows.label: MX Record
rows.value: Mail Exchange. Reveals email provider. aspmx.l.google.com = Google Workspace. mail.protection.outlook.com = Microsoft 365. Own server IP = real infrastructure, often NOT CDN-protected.

rows.label: NS Record
rows.value: Nameserver. Reveals DNS hosting provider. ns.cloudflare.com = Cloudflare. awsdns = AWS Route 53. Custom NS = self-managed DNS, possibly on-premises.

rows.label: TXT Record
rows.value: Email policies (SPF, DMARC, DKIM) and cloud service verification. DMARC p=none = domain CAN be spoofed. DMARC p=reject = domain is protected. Cloud service tokens reveal SaaS tools in use.

rows.label: CNAME Record
rows.value: Alias pointing to another domain. Reveals CDN (Cloudflare), SaaS platforms (Salesforce, HubSpot, Atlassian), and third-party hosting relationships. Each CNAME is a vendor disclosure.

rows.label: WHOIS
rows.value: Public registration record — registrant, creation date, expiry, registrar, nameservers. The internet's property deed. Query at who.is. Registrant may be hidden by privacy service.

rows.label: Registrar
rows.value: Company where domain was purchased (GoDaddy, Namecheap, Cloudflare Registrar). Accredited reseller. Submits registration to the registry on your behalf. NOT the same as the registry.

rows.label: Registry
rows.value: Organisation that operates a TLD's authoritative database (Verisign for .com, Nominet for .uk). Not a storefront — the official source of truth registrars submit to.

rows.label: TLD
rows.value: Top-Level Domain — the last segment (.com, .org, .uk). gTLD = generic. ccTLD = country-specific (reveals geographic jurisdiction). .gov/.edu = restricted to US government/education.

rows.label: ASN
rows.value: Autonomous System Number — unique ID for an organisation's IP network block. Reveals ALL IP ranges owned by the organisation. Lookup at bgp.he.net. The complete IP scope map.

rows.label: who.is / domaintools.com
rows.value: Domain WHOIS — registrant, dates, nameservers. DomainTools has historical WHOIS to find what was visible before privacy protection was enabled.

rows.label: dig / nslookup
rows.value: Command-line DNS query. dig MX target.com | dig TXT target.com | dig NS target.com (Linux/Mac). nslookup -type=MX target.com (Windows).

rows.label: mxtoolbox.com
rows.value: Web-based DNS, MX, TXT, and DMARC lookup. No installation. Fast. Useful for checking email security configuration.

rows.label: bgp.he.net
rows.value: ASN lookup and IP range discovery. Enter any IP address or organisation name to find their Autonomous System and full IP block ownership.

rows.label: viewdns.info
rows.value: Reverse IP lookup (all domains on a shared IP), historical DNS records, IP WHOIS. Passive. Useful for finding origin IPs behind CDNs.

rows.label: Step 1
rows.value: WHOIS lookup on the primary domain → record registrant, creation date, registrar, nameservers. Check for WHOIS privacy and note if enabled.

rows.label: Step 2
rows.value: DNS A record → IP address → IP WHOIS → confirm IP block owner (CDN or direct). If CDN, note the provider.

rows.label: Step 3
rows.value: DNS MX record → identify email provider → if self-hosted, run IP WHOIS on mail server IP.

rows.label: Step 4
rows.value: DNS TXT record → check SPF, DMARC policy (p=none/quarantine/reject), cloud service tokens.

rows.label: Step 5
rows.value: DNS NS record → identify DNS hosting provider.

rows.label: Step 6
rows.value: Check for typosquatting variants — missing/added hyphens, different TLDs, transposed letters. Any active mail server on a lookalike domain = immediate client notification.

rows.label: Step 7
rows.value: ASN lookup on known IPs → discover full IP range → map complete internet-facing scope.
